In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
decent work is a concept that can be applied in the Chinese apparel industry, but it is not fully understood and is often not achieved.

the study has identified the following key factors that affect decent work in the Chinese apparel industry: (1) workers’ attitudes toward decent work are significantly affected by their age, educational level, service length, monthly wage, and working hours; (2) workers have a low understanding of and low satisfaction with the primary indicators of decent working conditions; (3) workers increasingly value soft aspects and the overall work environment, not only financial aspects; (4) workers can be clustered into four different groups, and
this study provides an understanding of garment workers’ perceptions of decent work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the apparel industry is a key industry in China, and the industry is a significant contributor to China’s economic growth.
the Chinese apparel industry has been experiencing a rapid growth in the recent years, which is mainly due to the country’s low labor costs and the availability of a large pool of labor force.
the Chinese garment workers are not satisfied with the current working conditions, and the employers should take actions to improve the working conditions in terms of decent work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chinese apparel industry needs to focus on improving the overall work experience and work conditions, and not solely the financial benefits.
workers are more satisfied with soft factors than hard factors.
the apparel industry is not only an industry of economic value, but also one of human value.
